mechanism_narrative: The steady four-week narrowing of WORKPLACES mobility deficits from -22.1 to -12.0 signals a durable return of commuting routines; more weekday office presence mechanically raises nearby retail-and-recreation footfall, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than its mean over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing to improve or holding above -15.0.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean stays above +5.0, households remain in home-provisioning mode and divert spending from discretionary retail; this suppresses RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM > 5.0 for at least one weekly reading
regime_hint: steady state with elevated home provisioning
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days even though GROCERY_PHARM remains above +5.0.

mechanism_narrative: The latest sharp PARKS decline to -21.7 while TRANSIT improves to -25.1 indicates a substitution from outdoor park visits into indoor commercial transit-linked activity; this interaction lifts RETAIL_REC within one week.
regime_hint: reopening with park mobility displaced by weather or restrictions
failure_condition: In weeks where PARKS is below -20 and TRANSIT is above -30, RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a gradual reopening regime where RESIDENTIAL remains above +15, any decline in RESIDENTIAL toward +16 signals people spending less time at home; this releases trips to retail venues and raises RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
regime_hint: gradual reopening with residential mobility still above baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days falls or stays flat when RESIDENTIAL drops below 16.5.

mechanism_narrative: Policy easing is revealed by TRANSIT improving by more than 2 points week-on-week; as transit capacity and confidence recover, retail-and-recreation trips become easier, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by >2.0 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed its last 28-day mean when TRANSIT improves by more than 2 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A PARKS reading below -20 marks a seasonal shift away from outdoor recreation; displaced leisure demand moves to indoor retail-and-recreation venues, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week after PARKS prints below -20.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM stays above +5.0 and RESIDENTIAL falls below 17.0, households shift from home provisioning back to out-of-home discretionary spending, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
regime_hint: post-restriction rotation from essentials to discretionary spending
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not rise when GROCERY_PHARM is above +5.0 and RESIDENTIAL is below 17.0.

mechanism_narrative: Joint improvement in WORKPLACES above -15 and TRANSIT above -27 signals a coordinated reopening of offices and transport; this combination raises retail-and-recreation activity over four weeks.
regime_hint: coordinated reopening of workplaces and transit
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher when both WORKPLACES > -15 and TRANSIT > -27.
